previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and a history of TIPS placement and variceal bleeding, was admitted for post-procedure monitoring after undergoing radiofrequency ablation (RFA) of two liver tumors and a 4.5-liter paracentesis. He tolerated the procedure well with no immediate complications or evidence of bleeding. Post-procedure imaging revealed a new nonocclusive thrombus in the right axillary vein, which was evaluated with ultrasound. Due to recent bleeding risk, anticoagulation was not initiated, and management will be discussed with his specialist. His medications were continued, including those for hepatic encephalopathy and ascites, and he was discharged home the following day in stable condition with instructions to follow up on labs and the venous clot.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Acute embolism and thrombosis of right axillary vein

EXAMINATION:  CT CHEST W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  History: ___ with recent fall, AMS, HCV Cirrhosis s/p RFA with
pain to palpation of chest wall on R  // evaluate for rib fractures

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector helical scanning of the chest was performed without
intravenous contrast agent reconstructed as contiguous 5- and 1.25-mm thick
axial, 2.5-mm thick coronal and parasagittal, and 8 x 8 mm MIPs axial images

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 4.3 s, 33.6 cm; CTDIvol = 16.4 mGy (Body) DLP = 551.1
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 551 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  Chest CT dated ___ and ___

FINDINGS: 

The partially imaged thyroid gland is homogeneous.  There is a large
nonhemorrhagic right pleural effusion with associated atelectasis of the right
lower lobe.  The left lung is clear.  There is no supraclavicular or axillary
lymphadenopathy.  An enlarged subcarinal node measuring 1.1 cm in short axis
is unchanged from prior, possibly reactive.  The patient is status post CABG. 
Aorta and pulmonary arteries are normal size.

Limited views of the upper abdomen are notable for multiple hypodensities
within the liver which were better evaluated on contrast-enhanced CT abdomen
performed earlier the same day at outside institution.  The liver is
cirrhotic.  A TIPS stent is partially imaged, unable to evaluate patency
without contrast.  A hyperdense mass in the liver likely reflects prior TACE. 
The spleen is enlarged.  Ascites is partially imaged.  Note is made of
gynecomastia.  No displaced rib fracture is identified.

IMPRESSION:


1. No evidence of rib fracture.
2. Large right pleural effusion with associated right lower lobe atelectasis.
3. Limited views of the upper abdomen are notable for multiple hypodensities
within the cirrhotic liver which were better characterized on
contrast-enhanced CT abdomen performed earlier this same day at outside
institution.

COMPARISON:  Doppler ultrasound dated ___

FINDINGS: 

The liver appears diffusely coarsened and nodular consistent with known
cirrhosis.  Multiple lesions are again seen, which were better assessed on
recent MR abdomen.  There is trace ascites.  There is a a right pleural
effusion There is stable splenomegaly, with the spleen measuring 18.6 cm. 
There is cholelithiasis without evidence of cholecystitis.

The main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow.
The TIPS is patent and demonstrates wall-to-wall flow.
Portal vein and intra-TIPS velocities are as follows:
Main portal vein: 35 cm/sec, previously 30 cm/sec
Proximal TIPS: 366 cm/sec, previously 196cm/sec
Mid TIPS: 184 cm/sec, previously 259 cm/sec
Distal TIPS: 214  cm/sec, previously 216 cm/sec

Flow within the left portal vein is away from the TIPS shunt. Flow within the
right anterior and right posterior portal vein is  towards the TIPS. 
Appropriate flow is seen in the hepatic veins and IVC.

IMPRESSION:


1. Patent TIPS, but with interval change in intra-TIPS velocity with high
velocity in the proximal TIPS potentially worrisome for developing stenosis,
although this could be technical. Suggest short interval follow-up with
ultrasound in 1 to 2 weeks.
2. Trace ascites, decreased from prior
3. Multiple lesions within the liver which were better assessed on recent MRI.
4. Right pleural effusion

TECHNIQUE:  Ultrasound guided therapeutic and diagnostic thoracentesis

COMPARISON:  CT chest ___

FINDINGS: 

Limited grayscale ultrasound imaging of the right hemithorax demonstrated
moderate pleural fluid. A suitable target in the deepest pocket in the right
posterior mid scapular line was selected for thoracentesis.

PROCEDURE:  The procedure, risks, benefits and alternatives were discussed
with the patient and written informed consent was obtained.

A preprocedure time-out was performed discussing the planned procedure,
confirming the patient's identity with 3 identifiers, and reviewing a
checklist per ___ protocol.

Under ultrasound guidance, an entrance site was selected and the skin was
prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion. 1% lidocaine buffered with
sodium bicarbonate was instilled for local anesthesia.

A 5 ___ catheter was advanced into the largest fluid pocket in the right
posterior mid scapular line and 0.9 L of cloudy yellow fluid was removed.

The patient tolerated the procedure well without immediate complication.
Estimated blood loss was minimal.

Dr. ___ supervised the trainee during the key components of the
procedure and reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful ultrasound-guided thoracentesis.
